Cotton production 
*82.   SHRI   EKANATH   K.  T HAKUR:  Will   the   Minister  of 
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the production of cotton which was 14 million bales before, 
has come down to less than 9 million bales; 
(b) whether the cotton growers are in trouble in spite of Bt-cotton being 
grown in a substantial area; and 
(c) if so, the steps Government propose to take to improve the condition of 
cotton growers? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI RAJNATH SINGH): (a) to (c) 
A Statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha. 
Statement 
(a) to (c) The production of cotton during last three years is as below:—  
Year 2000-01 2001-02 2002-03 
Production (lakh bales of 
170 kg. each) 
95.24 100.94 93.10

                                     RAJYA SABHA            [25 July, 2003] 
The production declined in 2002-03 due to drought conditions in the* cotton 
growing area. Bt.-Cotton was grown for the first time during 2002-03 and 
covered a negligible area. 
 
Many steps have been taken to improve the production of cotton and the 
condition of cotton growers. These include: 
(i) The launch of Technology Mission on cotton in February, 2000. 
(ii) The announcement of a Minimum Support Price (MSP) every year. 
(iii) Protection against loss of cotton crop through National Agricultural 
Insurance Scheme, which is being implemented in 22 States and 2 
Union Territories for the benefit of both loanee and non loanee 
farmers.

heavy import of cotton during this particular period.

*83. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO: Will the Minister of SCIENCE 
AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Indian Meteorological Department has  started 
satellite based digital weather broadcast services to help the fishermen and 
seafarers; 
(b) if so, the details of the digital technology that is being used to help the 
fishermen; 
(c) whether this service can be used by other agencies; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN TH E DEPARTMENT OF SCIENCE 
AND TECHNOLOGY (SHRI BACHI SINGH RAWAT): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. 
Digital Data Broadcast has been started by the Indian Meteorological 
Department for seafarers. For fishermen, audio broadcast is needed, for which 
cheap and affordable receivers are being developed. The "Asia Sat" Satellite of 
M/s World Space Corporation having large coverage over Indian Ocean, Arabian 
Sea and Bay of Bengal is being used for the broadcast. These services of audio 
and multimedia products are provided using digital compression technology 
through-L Band Transponder. 
(c) and (d) This service can be used by several agencies like the

Review of working of Bharat Shiksha Kosh 
*85.SHRI R.P.GOENKA: 
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: 
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether Government have set up a Bharat Shiksha Kosh to make it a 
sole authority to receive and disburse funds donated by alumnus to their alma 
mater in India. 
(b) whether Government have reviewed the working of the Bharat 
Shiksha Kosh; 
(c) if so, the result thereof; 
(d) whether it is also a fact that due to such interception by Government in the 
flow of funds to IITs and IIMs, the wishes of the donors are not honoured and 
the donors are becoming hesitant to further donate; and 
(e) if so, the steps taken to allay the fears of the donors, especially the 
N.R.I's and also to clarify the role  of Government in utilising these 
contributions? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR. VALLABHBHAI RAMJIBHAI 
KATHIRIA): (a) to (e) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (e) The Bharat Shiksha Kosh has been constituted as a registered Society 
registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 to mobilize extra 
budgetary resources for educational development. The Kosh was 
16 

[25 July, 2003] RAJYA    SABHA 
launched on 9th January, 2003 during the celebrations of the Pravasi 
Bharatiya Diwas. The Government has made a one time contribution of Rs. 
1.00 crore to the Kosh. 
Instructions were issued on 21.2.2003 that all the institutions/ 
Autonomous bodies/Public Sector Undertakings under the Department of 
Secondary and Higher Education and the Department of Elementary 
Education and Literacy, which receive donations/grants from any external sources 
(other than Government support) for educational and research activities, shall 
get such donations/grants routed through the Bharat Shiksha Kosh. The donors 
would be requested to make such contributions to the Bharat Shiksha Kosh, which 
would, in turn, provide support for the activities as decided by the Kosh in 
consultation with the donor. 
The Kosh will fulfil the desires of the donors in utilising their contributions with 
accountability and as per their wishes. The Kosh permits sponsorships, under which 
any organisation or individual can become the sponsor (s) of the educational 
development of a particular village, town, city or of a school, college or even a 
single child through the payment of a specified amount. A school or college or 
any other institutions or even a building or block thereof may be named after the 
sponsor on payment of a prescribed amount. Chairs, prizes, scholarships and 
research projects in educational institutions could also be instituted in the names 
of the sponsors. 
In view of the above, there is no reason for any misgivings on the part of the 
donors that their wishes would not be honoured. The affairs of the Kosh are 
reviewed in the meetings of the Board of Governors.

Statement 
(a) and (b) Subsidy to urea manufacturers is being provided under the New 
Pricing Schemes (NPS) which has come into effect from 1.4.2003. Under the 
NPS, the urea units have been placed in six groups based on vintage and 
feedstock, for determining the group based concession rates. These groups are: 
pre-1992 gas based units, post-1992 ga s based units, pre-1992 naphtha based 
units, post-1992 naphtha based units, Fuel Oil/ Low Sulphur Heavy Stock 
(FO/LSHS) based units and mixed energy based units.The group based concession 
rates w.e.f. 1.4.2003 would be computed on the basis of the retention prices 
applicable as on 1.4.2002 duly updated for escalation/de-escalation in respect of 
feedstock, fuel, purchased power and water for the year 2002-03. 
Subsidy on decontrolled phosphatic and potassic fertilizers is given under 
the Concession Scheme. The concession rates for di-ammonium phosphate 
(DAP) are worked out for all the manufacturers after adjusting the imported 
ammonia and imported phosphoric acid prices prevailing in the international 
market. Rates of concession for comple x fertilizers are worked out after 
adjusting the nutrients cost based on the raw materials, ammonia, urea, 
phosphoric acid prices prevailing in the international market and naphtha prices 
prevailing in the indigenous market. Manufacturers of single super phosphate 
(SSP) are provided subsidy uniformly at the rate of Rs. 650 per metric ton. 
(c) The NPS for urea and the methodology of calculating the rates of 
concession for decontrolled phosphatic and potassic. fertilizers have been 
adopted to ensure greater transparency, efficiency and uniformity and to allow 
fair price to the manufacturers/ suppliers of these fertilizers.

Data on Railway Bridges 
*81. SHRI K. KALAVENKATA RAO: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether CAG has warned that the absence of data on construction of 
over one lakh railway bridges may hamper their monitoring; and 
(b) if so, the remedial measures proposed to be taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF RAILWAYS (SHRI NITISH KUMAR): (a) No, 
Sir. CAG has only observed that date of construction of some bridges is not 
available with some Railways and this may hamper their monitoring. 
(b) The year of opening of line ha s been adopted as the year of 
construction of the bridges. The Bridges Inspection Register record is 
accordingly under updation.  However, rehabilitation/rebuilding of bridges 
does not depend merely on the age of the bridges, but on the physical 
condition as ascertained during the inspection of the bridges for which, a well 
laid down multitier annual inspection procedure for each and every bridge 
exists. The distressed bridges are inspected more frequently. 
All the old Cast Iron Pile Foundation Bridges and Bridges with Early 
Steel Superstructure have been sanctioned for rebuilding. All distressed 
bridges are sanctioned for rehabilitation/rebuilding each year as continuous 
process. 
Action has also been taken for modernization of Bridge Inspection and 
Management System as per details given in Para 2.4.5 of the White Paper   on 
Railway   Safety which has been laid in the Rajya 
48 

[25 July, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
Sabha on 07.04.2003. It is planned to make the existing inspection and 
monitoring systems more scientific as detailed in above para by importing 
modern technology for inspection and assessment of condition of bridges by 
using. 
(i) Under water Inspections. 
(ii) Mapping   unknown     foundations and integrity testing   of-
foundations. 
(iii) Non-Destructive Testing Techniques like Ultra Sonics, Acoustic 
Emission, Strain Gauging and Radar etc. 
(iv) Fatigue    life and residual life   assessment techniques. 
(v) Modern Bridges   Management   System. 
Pilot projects for items (i) to (v) of above activities have been 
sanctioned. Purchase of Non-destru ctive testing equipment has been 
sanctioned for setting up of mobile testing laboratories over 9 Zonal 
Railways    at a cost of 12.7 crores this year.

2. The Reserve Bank of India in consultation with the Government

The Reserve Bank of India in consultation with the Government has 
issued Standing Guidelines for providing relief to the farmers in areas affected 
by natural calamities. These guidelines include, inter alia, the following 
measures: 
I. Convert/reschedule loans in th e event of natural calamity for 
periods ranging from 3 to 9 years depending upon the successive 
crop failure/intensity of damage of crops. 
II. Grant fresh crop loans to affected farmers. 
III. Convert principal as well as interest due on the existing loans. 
IV. Grant of consumption loans. 
V. Not to compound interest in respect of loans converted/ rescheduled. 
VI. Not to charge penal interest in respect of current dues in default. 
In addition, the RBI/NABARD has advised the banks to extend specific 
credit related relief measures to the drought affected farmers of the country 
following the announcement made by the Hon'ble Prime Minister on 14th 
November, 2002. These measures include the following: 
I. There should be no recovery of any amount either by way of principal 
of interest during the current financial year in respect-of Kharif crop 
loan. 
II. The principal amount of crop loan should be converted into 
term loan and will be recovered over a period of minimum five 
years in the case of small and ma rginal farmers and four years 
in the case of other farmers (as against three years stipulated 
in the existing guidelines). 
III. Interest due in the current financial year on crop loan should also be 
deferred. No interest should be charged on the deferred interest.

affected States, the first year's deferred liability of interest on Kharif loan has 
been waived as a one time measure.

594. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA: Will the Minister of 
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be pleased to state: 
95 

RAJYA  SABHA [25 July, 2003] 
(a) whether All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) threatened to launch agitation 
if the Centre do not ban transgenic hybrid varieties including Bt. Cotton in the 
country in view of their harmful effects on environment and people; 
(b) if so, the views of Government on use of genetically modified seeds; 
and 
(c) the action taken by Government to compensate farmers who incurred 
losses by opting Bt. Cotton? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT 
AND FORESTS (SHRI DILIP SINGH JUDEV): (a) No, Sir. 
(b) and (c) The Government is following a policy of case by case 
approval of transgenic crops. Bt. cotton is the only transgenic crop approved for 
commercial cultivation in India. The Genetic Engineering Approval 
Committee (GEAC) accorded conditional approval for commercial cultivation 
of three Bt. Cotton varieties namely MECH-12, MECH-162 and MECH-184 of 
M/s Mahyco Hybrid Seed Company Ltd. in April, 2002 for a period of three 
years. During Kharif 2002, some of th e Bt. cotton fields were monitored by 
the Committees constituted by this Ministry. The Comm ittees observations 
and discussion with farmers indicated that the performance of Bt. Cotton is 
satisfactory as compared to its non Bt. counterpart. However, the yield of 
cotton crop (both in Bt. and Non-Bt. Hybrid), has been severely affected due 
to severe drought conditions during Kharif 2002. In view of the varying agro 
climatic conditions it has been decided to assess the performance of during a 
period of three years.

UNESCO has brought out a EFA Global Monitoring Report, 2002 in which India

Education and Total Literacy by 2015. The conclusions drawn in this Report are 
based on data available to UNESCO on the parameters of net enrolment ratio in 
primary schools, gender parity as per gross enrolment ratio in primary schools and 
the percentage of audit literacy. The data used by UNESCO for these parameters 
were either outdated or not available to UNESCO as far as I ndia is concerned.

of elementary education. The objectives of SSA are :

'Back-to-School' camp by 2003 
— All children complete five years of primary schooling by 2007 
— All children complete eight years of elementary schooling by 2010 
— Focus on elementary education of satisfactory quality with emphasis 
on education for life

and at elementary education level by 2010

colleges;

uncontrolled trade in professional education field; 
(c) whether it is a fact that the private colleges have resorted to this 
practice misinterpreting a Supreme Court judgement of December, 2002 freeing 
unaided private colleges from Government fee control; and 
(d) if so, what is Government's reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR.  VALLABHBHAI RAMJIBHAI

(b) to (d) As per the judgement of Hon'ble Supreme Court dated 31st 
October, 2002 in the T.M.A. Pai Foundation & Others Versus State of 
Karnataka and Others Case, in professional un-aided institutions, a rational fee 
structure should be adopted by the Management, which would not be entitled to 
charge a capitation fee. Appropriate machinery can be devised by the State or 
University to ensure that no capitation fee is charged and that there is no 
profitering, though institutions may be permitted to accumulate a reasonable 
surplus for furtherance of education. Accordingly, an Interim Policy Regulation 
was notified by AICTE on 20th March, 2003, according to which, State 
Governments are to decide a fee structrue for the Institutions in the respective 
State for the academic year 2003-04. The Ministry of Health and Family

653. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH : Will the Minister of HUMAN

(a) whether it is a fact that Government had introduced a scheme in 
1993-94 to teach a South Indian language in Hindi speaking States and UTs; 
(b) if so, the number of South Indian languages i.e. Telugu, Tamil, 
Kannada and Malayalam which were introduced, number of teachers 
appointed and the amount spent on each  language, since the inception of

RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (DR.  VALLABHBHAI RAMJIBHAI 
KATHIRIA): (a) and (b) The Government of India launched a Scheme called 
Appointment of Modern Indian Language Teachers (MIL) in 1993-94 with the 
objective of implementation of Three Language Formula and promoting 
national integration as well as to help the development of composite Hindi by 
drawing on from the regional languages as envisaged in the Constitution. 
Under the scheme a grant was releas ed to the Government of Haryana 
and to the Government of Himachal Pradesh in the year 1994-95.13 Tamil 
teachers had been appointed by the Government of Himachal Pradesh to teach 
Tamil in the schools of the State. In the 10th plan the scheme is being 
implemented under a wider scheme of Appointment of Language Teachers.

Training and Supervision in Railways 
662. SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that 65 per cent of the causes of train accidents are 
attributed to human error; 
(b) whether this reflects a low standa rd of training and supervision in 
Railways; and 
(c) if so, what are Government views on this? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(SHRI BANDARU DATTATRAYA): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) and (c) NO, Sir. This does not reflect low standards of training on 
Railways. Indian Railways is a vast organization employing about 15.15 lakh 
staff and in the fact of safety considerations and manpower variety, training on 
the Railways is given a very high priority. All staff, including safety category 
staff, are properly trained before extensive utilization of newly acquired 
technological aids is adopted. Modifying and refreshing the training of 
Railway staff to update their knowledge and skill is a continuous process. A 
comprehensive training need analysis of all categories of staff is carried out 
and training modules are revised to suit the changes in technology, work 
practices and objectives of the job. Additional funds have also been allotted to 
the training centres for upgradation of training facilities. 
Ultrasonic Flaw Detection Test during Monsoon 
663. SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: Will the Minister of 
RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is mandatory for Railways to periodically patrol and 
176 

[25 July, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
run checks, including 'Ultrasonic Flaw Detection Test", on the Railway tracks, 
particularly during monsoon seasons and areas prone to heavy rainfall, 
landslides and shifting of land; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is a fact that Konk an Railway Corporation had not 
undertaken the regular checks, including netting of the vulnerable areas, 
resulting in the recent accident on the Karwar-Ratnagiri Sector; and 
(d) if so, what measures are being cont emplated to ensure compliance of 
safety exercises by the Railways for prevention of accidents? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(SHRI BANDARU DATTATRAYA): (a) and (b) Patrolling of Railway Track is 
carried out in identified sections, in accordance with extant instructions which 
cover all seasons including monsoon. Ultrasonic Flaw Detection Test is 
carried out on rails on need based concept, unrelated to season. 
(c) No, Sir. Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd. had undertaken regular 
checks including netting of the vulner able areas. The site of accident 
was, however, not considered vulnerable by the Expert Committee. 
(d) Railways are continuously st riving to prevent accidents and 
measures, being taken for ensuring compliance, include training of staff, 
safety awareness campaign, safety drives, monsoon precautions includng. 
identification of vulnerable spots and monsoon patrolling.

the Candidate Vaccine for AIDS is under development under the National Jai

Elimination of subsidy by OECD 
707. SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE : Will the Minister of STEEL be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether OECD (Organisation of Economic Cooperation and 
Development) has proposed to eliminate all specific subsidy for the steel 
industries for curbing the market distortions in international trade in steel; 
(b) if so, what would be its impact on Indian steel industries; and 
(c) whether India has made any effort to ensure support of other steel 
exporting countries like Brazil, Egypt, etc; if so, what are their response? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STEEL (SHRI 
BRAJ KISHORE TRIPATHY) (a) At the initiative of the OECD c ountries 
with interest in international steel trade have been deliberating upon issues 
relating to effectiveness of existing multilateral disciplines on market 
distorting measures relevant for trade in the steel sector.The proponents of the 
OECD steel deliberations are of the view that subsidies and related government 
support have caused and are causing significant distortions in the steel markets 
and these will be required to be reduced and where possible eliminated. 
Elements of a possible Steel Subsidy Agreement are being discussed by the 
participating countries. 
(b) While remaining engaged in the negotiating process, India is 
primarily trying to preserve the special and differential treatment provisions 
available to the developing countries under the existing WTO Agreement on 
Subsidies and Countervailing Measures.These provisions enable India to provide 
crucial export incentives to the industry, and if these are preserved, there is 
not likely to be any significant impact on the Indian steel industry. 
(c) Yes, Sir. However, there is divergen ce in the core interests of Egypt, 
Brazil and India. While India has been essentially trying to preserve the flexibility 
to provide export incentives available under Acticle 27 of the WTO 
Agreement on Subsidies ana Countervailing Measures. Egypt's main interest is 
protecting its ability to provide assistance for re-structuring of the steel industry 
including its privatisation. Brazil's core interest lie in protecting their ability to 
provide assistance to correct deficiencies  in their financial markets and aid to 
disadvantaged regions.

708.    SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY: 
SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO:  
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that to protect the Indian steel industry, which is 
passing through rough weather, Government are thinking of enacting Buy 
Indian Steel Act; and 
(b) if so, the salient features of the proposed legislation? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STEEL (SHRI 
BRAJ KISHORE TRIPATHY): (a) Yes, Sir. A proposal to enact "Buy Indian 
Act" is under consideration of the Government. However, it may be noted 
that the proposal was mooted at a time  when the domestic industry had been 
passing through a severe crisis caused by low price and poor demand. The 
situation has shown improvement since January 2002 with the price of steel 
products on an increase and a fair amount of stability having been achieved. 
(b) Some of the salient features of the proposed legislation are as 
follows: 
(i) Every public work or industry established or run with the aid or 
assistance of public funds shall procure its requirment of iron and steel 
material from indigenous manufacturers unless use of such material is: 
(a) to be made outside India,. (b) to be contrary to public interest of 
detrimental to the project, (c) not available indigenously in specified 
quality or within the required delivery schedule. 
(ii) Every contract for construction, modification, modernisation, 
installation, alteration or repairs or any public works or industrial 
establishment, which is being undertaken with assistance from the 
public fund should contain a provision that for the performance and 
execution of the job, the person responsible shall use only such un-
manufactured or manufactured iron and steel material which have 
been mined, produced or manufactured within the country unless it is 
impracticable for successful completion of the work.

requiring procurement of iron and steel material from sources outside the 
provision of the Act shall furnish a declaration in the prescribed format to 
the head of the department/organisation/agency/ contractor. The 
Authority to whom such declaration is submitted, shall examine the 
same and if found essential for the completion or execution of the work, 
forward the same to the Secretary of the concerned Department of

sports persons from use of any kind of prohibited drugs. During the coaching 
camps, strict instructions have been i ssued to the coaches attached with the 
campers to educate and regularly counsel and players about the banned drugs.

banned substances.The list of banned drugs and placards for education of players

searched and checked at regular intervals to see that no banned drugs are used 
besides testing the urine samples of sports persons during

GOVERNMENT MOTION 
For consideration of progress of implementation of Part IX and Part IX-
A of Constitution (contd.) 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS AND THE 
MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION 
(MAJ. GEN. (RETD.) B.C. KHANDURI): Mr. Chairman, Sir, I rise to intervene 
briefly in the discussion on the review of ten years of implementation of Part 
IX-A of the Constitution relating to the urban local bodies. My Ministry, that is, the 
Urban Development and Poverty Alleviation Ministry, of which I am holding 
the additional charge, circulated a background note giving the present status of 
the implementation of Part IX-A of the Constitution as regards urban local 
bodies, that is, the Municipalities. We have circulated a background note 
where we have given some of the data, 
233 

RAJYA  SABHA [25 July, 2003] 
which are available from the States, with regard to the implementation of the 
various directions given in the Seventy-fourth Amendments which was 
implemented from 1st of June, 1993. 
Sir, I am thankful to the speakers who raised various issues yesterday with 
regard to the implementation of the provisions of Part IX-A of the 
Constitution. Most of the speakers dwelt basically on the Panchayats. but all 
those problems, which were highlighted, relating to the Panchayats like non-
implementation of provisions of Part-IX A devolution of power, financial 
viability of the local bodies, are also  applicable to the urban local bodies, that 
is, the Municipalities. Therefore, I am thankful to all the Members who have 
highlighted those areas and I am quite sure that we will be benefited by them. 
The main provisions of the Act, as regards the urban local bodies, are also given 
on pages 3 to 9 of the background note which we have circulated. Basically, we 
have highlighted 12 items which needed urgent implementation. Yesterday, a 
number of speakers highlighted various shortcomings about implementation 
with regard to the Panchayats. As I said, these are also applicable. Shri Venkaiah 
Naidu gave a very detailed and very brilliant analysis of various problems and 
also suggested remedy for overcoming these maladies. A number of other 
Members also highlighted various issues. I am quite sure, with that analysis and 
with those suggestions, we will be able to move forward. I personally am in 
entire agreement with what has been said both about the non-devolution of real 
powers to the local bodies as also the financial non-viability of all these 
institutions which causes problems so far as the implementation is concerned. I, 
therefore, feel that we need do a major surgery for the implementation of 
provisions. Minor tinkering and minor remedial measures will not help. 
So far as the Ministry of Urban Development and Poverty Alleviation is 
concerned, we had tried to interact with the State Government. We have had a 
number of meetings. We had made a number of suggestions with regard to 
implementation. Unfortunately, both the real devolution of power and financial 
delegation have not found favour. In the Background Paper, we have indicated 
the response of various States in regard to various provisions. We have not 
been very successful. However, we continue to put in our efforts. The data 
pertaining to our success or failure has been given in Annexures 1 to 5 to the 
Background Paper. 
234 

[25 July, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
(THE DEPUTY CHAIRMAN in the Chair) 
During this period, the Tenth Finance Commission and the Eleventh 
Finance Commission have also made certain provisions to help the local bodies. 
The Tenth Finance Commission had given Rs. 1,000 corres and the Eleventh 
Finance Commission has given Rs. 2,000 crores. I agree that this sum is 
inadequate. But it is a beginning. Ultimately, this also has to find its way 
right down to the local bodies, which normally does not happen in all cases for 
some reason or the other. At the Central level, we have been trying to improve 
the functioning of the local bodies by making various suggestions. The 
Ministry of Urban Development and Poverty Alleviation has nine such 
schemes which I would put across to the States. Some progress has already been 
made.These schemes are: 
(1) Integrated Development of Small and Medium Towns, (IDSMT) 
(2) Infrastructure development in Mega Cities; (3) Accelerated Urban Water 
Supply Programme, (AUWSP); (4) Low Cost Sanitation Scheme for 
Liberation of Scavengers; (5) Swar najayanti Shahari Rojgaar Yojana, 
(SJSRY); (6) Shelter and Sanitation Facilities for the Footpath Dwellers 
in Urban Areas; (7) National Network of  Building Centres; (8) Additional 
Central Assistance to States for Slum Development—National slum 
Development Programme and (9) The Balmiki Ambedkar Awas Yojana 
(VAMBAY). 
In conclusion, I would only like to say that from the Central 
Government side, we will continue to make efforts to see that the local and 
urban bodies function efficiently. Th ere are a number of problems and 
obstacles which had been adequately highlighted yesterday. I think it is time 
which all of us should try and make efforts. Although it is a State subject and 
the ultimate delegation has to be done by the State, but it is the responsibility of 
all of us here to do whatever possible we can do to see that this system functicns 
efficiently. I hope after today's debate in both the Houses, the State Govenrments 
would be encouraged to do further real devolution of power as well as financial 
delegation so that the system functions efficiently. 
Madam, I thank you for having given me this opportunity to highlight the 
viewpoint of the Ministry of Urban Development and Poverty Alleviation.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOP-
MENT (SHRI ANNASAHEB M.K.PATIL): Madam, this agust House had 
witnessed a lively debate on the Motion pertaining to the implementation of the 
Seventy-third and Seventy-fourth amendments. A number of eminent 
Members, particularly those who had been in villages, have expressed their 
views and gave many good suggestions in order to have a good system of 
functioning of the PRIs. 
Shri Pranab Mukherjee initiated the debate, and Shri Venkaiah Naidu, 
elaborated in detail the subjects including all the activities and points 
pertaining to PRIs. Madam, it is no doubt an idea initiated by Mahatma 
Gandhi, then carried out by Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya, Chowdhuryji and 
even by Shri Rajiv Gandhi. But, whatev er has been experienced by the hon. 
Members with regard to the functioning of these PRIs in the past ten years have 
been mentioned by them in their speeches. 
Broadly, the major aspects which were dealt with by most of the 
Members include transfer of ail 29 subjects to PRIs with funds, functions and 
functionaries. This has to be a very vital and an important aspect of the 
Panchayati Raj system. Madam, you will note that some of the States have already 
taken steps in this direction. I would, particularly, name the State of Karnataka; 
whether it is only on paper or it is an actual fact; I do not know. It has been 
brought to our notice that they have already implemented all the 29 subjects 
with funds, functions and functionaries. While a few States are midway in 
this, many of the states have taken some steps starting from one or two 
subjects to almost all the subjects. Many States have taken about 11 subjects. 
And, the Committee appointed by the hon. Prime Minister called the 
Empowered Sub-Committee, to deal with all the aspects of the Panchayati 
Raj Institution system has taken about 11 subjects which can be made 
common to all the States. One meeting was already held and there were very 
fruitful discussions in that meeting, and we expect that the next meeting will be 
held on 2nd of August this year. 
Regarding funds, functions and functionaries, some Members have stated 
that unless funds are with the PRIs, nothing  can be done. It is a fact. In some 
places, we find that powers are with them, but there is no fund, and hence they 
are not able to do anything. Therefore, we agree with this view of the hon. 
Members. The second point was evolution of 
236 

[25 July, 2003] RAJYA   SABHA 
powers independently without interference of the States. Many Members have 
suggested that there is a lot of encroachment by the States on the powers of the 
Panchayati Raj institutions. Some States are not allowing the elected 
representatives, Zila Presidents as Chairmen of the District Planning 
Committees, and making some Ministers or even some other men as chairmen 
of those Committees. These are also to be noted. Madam, I can say that the 
Central Government is very particular that all the elected representatives should

Water scarcity in the country 
SHRIMATI SHABANA AZMI (Nomin ated): Madam, a recent World 
Water Development Report ranked India a lowly 133rd among 188 countries 
in terms of water availability and 120th among 122 in terms of water quality. 
Water scarcity in India is largely man made. It is the result of a 
shortsighted pricing policy for public water supply that encourages wasteful 
use of water and makes it difficult to raise resources for upkeep and 
expansion of the system. 
India has 2.45 per cent of the world's land and 4 per cent of its fresh water 
resources. India's annual precipitation, snowfall and rain, is 4,000 billion cubic 
metre. This translates into 1869 BCM of water in river of which barely is 
used. Thus 1179 BCM of water flows into the sea. Add 432 BCM of 
groundwater the real availability of water is 1122 BCM which is sufficient to 
meet the needs of water of this country. 
We had prepared Five Year Plans for solution of water problem but the 
projects are ill funded and not completed. As of 2001, 159 major projects, 251 
medium ones and 94 renovation works have been pending since the 1960s. 
Keeping in view, therefore, we need to create autonomous and 
decentralized organisations with signifi cant user participation for setting up, 
financing and managing individual irrigation and domestic water supply systems. 
I, therefore, urge the Government should consider to take concrete 
measures and implement that so that  the problem of water is removed 
immediately.
